Oh, my baby, he's going to be ina lor of pain, is it?

Your anxiety is understandable. However, try not to be too concerned
about this as the pain-killers will be very effective in alleviating his
pain.

Bur, can it reoccur? What are the chances of it happening again?

The doctor believes thar Jimmy's tumour is noncancerous and these
kinds of tumours don't come back once they have been removed,
causing no further problems, Having said thar, the doctor will repeat
MRI tests in some of your follow-up appointments to monitor
Jimmy's condition

Ok. But, my greatest fear at the moment is abour this tumour’s effect
on Jimmy's cognitive abilities. Will it have a long-term impact on his
brain?

As with any surgery, it will ake some time to recover, and Jimmy may
experience problems with physical abilities, behaviour, or speech
difficulties. Bur, we will provide support with overcoming any
problems that he may have,

Still, tell me more about the options that would be available for me. |
am a single parent, and I don't know whether | will be able to provide
the required care.

Right, | do understand what you mean. At the time of discharge, you
will be provided with detailed written and verbal instructions about
the transition to care at home. Also, Occupational Therapists, Physical
therapists, speech therapists, and Visiting Nurses will be able to assist
Jimmy in transitioning to healing after discharge if required.

Hmm, | have been a terrible mother. | am so busy with work. Had |
taken more care, Jimmy would have been fine today.

Don't blame yourself, Mrs Anderson, The exact cause of a tumour is
unknown; therefore, you do not have to feel responsible for in. |
understand thar the news has stunned you, and you are under a lot of
pressure, bur looking after yourself is also necessary. Let me explain, if
you are healthier, you will be able to help and support in a beer way.
Does that make sense to you?

You are right, but I still can’t come to terms with it. Ir's all happened

so suddenly.

Yes, | do understand that it's going to take some time to absorb this
information, We are going to be with you and Jimmy every step of the
way. Moreover, | can refer you co some local support groups where
you will be able to connect with caregivers of people who have
survived brain tumours. This will be an excellent opportunity for you
to understand their experiences.

Yes, speaking to other parents might help. | would appreciate thar.

It's nor a problem Mrs Anderson. | will check on Jimmy's condition
and will be back shortly co take you to his room.
